The file itself decides this one.

**What the STEP holds:** one `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`, imported as a single `Solid`, 7 faces, OCCT reports it valid. Bounding box 0–200 × 0–100 × 0–100 in file units, volume 1.7487e6 file-units³; there is one `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` of radius 20 in it. Geometrically it is a clean, closed, single-solid part and would mesh without complaint.

**Why I am not meshing it:** its length unit is not declared. The global unit context `#425` references `#426 = ( LENGTH_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) );` — a length unit with neither an `SI_UNIT(...)` prefix/name nor a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT` conversion factor. The other two units in the same context *are* declared (`SI_UNIT($,.RADIAN.)`, `SI_UNIT($,.STERADIAN.)`), so this is not a reader quirk on my side or a whole-context omission; the length unit specifically carries no scale. build123d/OCCT will hand back the raw numbers regardless, which is exactly the failure mode that hides: 200 could be 200 mm or 200 m, and OpenFOAM would read whatever I wrote as metres either way. The mesh would look perfect at either scale and be wrong by a factor of 1000 in length, 10⁹ in volume, 10³ in Reynolds number, with nothing downstream able to see it.

Guessing millimetres because "CAD is usually millimetres" is the one assumption I cannot record honestly, because it is indistinguishable from a stated fact once the mesh exists. This needs one line back from the customer: what unit are the coordinates in. With that, this part is a straightforward single-solid prepare-and-mesh and I would scale once on import and carry on.
